text.1: A robot sees nothing like that.
text.2: Point a camera at this room and what the robot actually receives is a grade of numbers.
text.4: Every pixel in the screen is just a brightness from 0 for black and 255 for white.
text.5: One Full HD frame holds over 6 million of these.
text.6: At 30 frames a second, that's nearly 200 million numbers every single second.
text.7: And not one of them says drone.
text.8: So the robot has to find the meaning itself.
text.10: Shapes that adds up to an object.
text.11: And clues to how far away each one is.
text.12: That leap from raw numbers to understanding the world is what we call a perception.
text.13: Without it, a robot can't find the gap, dodge any obstacle, land, or anything like that.
text.14: To learn more, read Fundamentals of Robot Perception by Braids Lab.
